title: EVM Benchmarks
body:
_(Edited)_

We've benchmarked the Wako EVM upgrade using the [raymond.release](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/tree/raymond.release) branch, focusing on the EVM pallet.

The benchmark results are that 1 unit of EVM gas = 3000-4000 picoseconds of execution time, which means the amount of EVM gas we can process per second = 250,000,000.

So far we have conservatively configured gas per second = 8,000,000, which means our block gas limit is 12m gas (Ethereum's is 15m gas). The benchmark suggests we could raise that amount significantly to 250,000,000, which would mean our block gas limit is 375m.

On Beresheet we'll set the block gas limit to 225m, but I recommend running the deploy to mainnet with a gas limit of 12m and will cut a release for v3.3.4 accordingly.

We're going to execute an upgrade to Beresheet that raises the allowable gas per second, and then test for stability by running a few scripts to pack the testnet with blocks. In the meantime we can choose to proceed with the Wako upgrade using the currently configured parameters.

---

To replicate the benchmarks:
cargo build --release --features=runtime-benchmarks

target/release/edgeware benchmark --pallet "pallet_evm" --extrinsic "runner_execute" --repeat 100 --wasm-execution compiled --output /tmp/

cat /tmp/pallet_evm.rs
Results:
/// Weight functions for pallet_evm.
pub struct WeightInfo<T>(PhantomData<T>);
impl<T: frame_system::Config> pallet_evm::WeightInfo for WeightInfo<T> {
        fn runner_execute(x: u32, ) -> Weight {
                (0 as Weight)
                        // Standard Error: 0
                        .saturating_add((4_000 as Weight).saturating_mul(x as Weight))
                        .saturating_add(T::DbWeight::get().reads(2 as Weight))
                        .saturating_add(T::DbWeight::get().writes(1 as Weight))
        }
}
